Didn't ask about additional rooms (garage, storage unit, balcony) beyond the general house-vs-condo question
Didn't ask about special considerations like narrow hallways, tight turns, or long carries at the destination
Didn't ask about storage stops or additional stops
Didn't ask about access concerns (parking, HOA restrictions, elevator)
No explicit moving-stressors question (e.g. "anything you're particularly worried about with this move?")
Didn't fully itemize what's included in the hourly rate — mentioned dollies, hand trucks, and tools, but not wrap pads/bands, taxes, or insurance
Never mentioned No Worries Damage Coverage (up to $2,000 protection)
Never mentioned Meet Your Mover (photo + info email before the move)
Never mentioned the On-Time Guarantee (discount if the crew misses the arrival window)

Didn't give a typical time range for a move this size — only cited the 2.5-hour minimum
Acknowledged the heavy antique table but didn't explain how a specialty item could affect time or pricing
Didn't address walk distance from the truck to the rooms/floors
Skipped the entire Save Your Ass prep speech — no consolidation tip for the ~20 loose totes, no "take a carload" tip, no closing sense-check
Never explicitly stated that no deposit is required to book
Didn't state Einstein's hours or a direct way to reach the branch beyond "give us a ring"
No genuine rapport-building or humor moment beyond baseline warmth/politeness
Never explained insurance/damage protection specifics (No Worries coverage + 60¢/lb baseline)

top_strength: Jespah built a complete, accurate picture of the job (stairs, furniture list, ~20 totes) through natural conversation and used it to give a confident quote and lock in the booking on the spot with no back-and-forth.
coaching_note: The biggest miss is Section 6 — she skipped the Save Your Ass prep speech entirely; with ~20 loose totes in play she had a natural opening to tell Morgan to consolidate small items before move day to protect the 2.5-hour minimum, and should make that speech a habit on every call regardless of job size.
phone_presence_notes: Consistently warm, conversational language with repeated affirmations and natural use of the customer's name, though no standout humor or explicit customer praise that would push it to Outstanding.
